comment: It covers K1–K5: all 11 production call sites, the 4 test/e2e sites, the 9 second-level sites in stateful_set_control.go, the kubectl version as a separate function, and the option of adding a new function. Its extra point, that nextPodAvailabilityCheck is used by RS/SS via FindMinNextPodAvailabilityCheck, is also correct. The only flaw is the count: it says 17 call sites, but there are 16.

The direct callers, the second-level sites, the kubectl version as a separate function, and the nextPodAvailabilityCheck note are all correct, including the ginkgo.It at line 644. But it gets the count wrong (17 instead of 16) and claims tests like stateful_set_utils_test.go call the wrappers, when no test does. It gives a next step (go build) but doesn't suggest adding a new function.

It covers K1–K4 and gives scope estimates at three levels. But it says 17 call sites when there are 16, and says nextPodAvailabilityCheck is used by 'ReplicaSet and Deployment' when the actual users are ReplicaSet and StatefulSet. It doesn't suggest the new-function approach.

The call-site tables and the separation of the kubectl version are correct. But its stated counts (20 total, 12 production, 8 test) contradict its own tables; the real numbers are 16, 11 and 5. It also doesn't suggest a new function or other alternative.

It covers K1–K5, including the new-function proposal, and correctly spots that the kubectl version's boundary check differs (Before vs Compare<=0), which is a nice extra. But its counts are wrong (20 total, 12 production), and it claims stateful_set_control_test.go has one call to the wrappers when that line is only a comment.

The direct callers with their enclosing functions, the 9 second-level sites, nextPodAvailabilityCheck, and the kubectl version are all correct. But it says 19 call sites when there are 16, and it doesn't suggest a new function or other alternative.
